title: The Signalman Who Was a Baboon

camera_idea.name: He never looks up
camera_idea.why: Jack runs the junction by ear and never lifts his eyes, so the camera does the looking for him: it lives at the baboon's eye height at his levers, and every time something arrives above him (the cab, the lady's window, the tall inspector) it looks up and comes back down to the same calm face.
camera_idea.signature: On 'he doesn't even look up' the camera, for once, does not look up either: it stays on Jack while the train shakes the frame; then it leaves its post for the only time, runs down the line with the last train to the inspector and his notes, and on 'You see' rises over the whole junction before it sinks back to Jack's ear.

letters.kind: paper letters fluttering out of the carriage windows (fx)

tracks.kind: main line and branch at the points (set)

rigs.subject_path: object_path of the train mover, cab -70 -> 0.0 on the main line
rigs.recipe: catch from the lever frame: the camera rises from Jack's eye height and tilts up as the engine slides in behind the levers; whistle steam on the word; no kick (it stops, it does not hit)

rigs.action: pass 1 of 'train after train' (seen, going away east)
rigs.recipe: the camera holds the three-shot low beside Jack; the train enters over the left shoulder 5 m away and recedes up the frame (follow-away, no pan); kick 7 f amp 1.2 on 'train'; motion blur on the train only
static medium on Jack and his lever; the train fills the top of the frame behind him for about 12 f; kick amp 1.5 on 'toots'; flash of whistle steam; Jack does not react
static medium on Jack and the key; same as pass 2, kick on 'toots'; the slow creep toward Jack's face keeps going through the pass: the camera does not look up

rigs.action: the last train; the camera leaves its post
rigs.recipe: chase: the camera lets the engine overtake at Jack's shoulder, then runs east beside the wheels 1 m up for 14 m (the travel into 'checking', 2.3 s), carriages streaming past on the left; catch: it slows to a stop on the boardwalk and turns back to find the inspector; kick amp 2.5 on 'up' as the engine passes the lens

rigs.action: a train comes up the main line and stops before the points (seen from above)
rigs.recipe: crane: the camera is already high over the boardwalk (rise on 'see'); it holds while the train comes toward it, 2 whistle puffs on 'whistled' and on 'times'; then a forward glide to the high view of both tracks on 'track'

rigs.action: 'lost both his legs under a train' (heard, not seen)
rigs.subject_path: point: the signalman in his trolley
rigs.recipe: kick 7 f amp 1.5 and a red flash <= 2 f on 'train'; no train moves

takes.cut_in: hidden: time passes. A wall calendar drops over the frame on 'by the end of the month', its days flip to 30, the last page tears away on the lever frame
hidden: whistle steam whites out the frame for 4 f on each side of the cut (the inspector leaves by train)
hidden: through the story object. The office take ends pushed into the cream letter on the desk; this take starts on the same letter in the signalman's hand and pulls back

sentences.text: A signalman ran a busy railway junction for nine years, and he never said a single word.
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: His owner lost both his legs under a train, so he can't reach his own levers anymore.
sentences.subject: wide

sentences.text: So he buys a baboon at the market, and he calls him Jack.
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: Every morning Jack pushes him to work on a little trolley along the rails,
sentences.subject: wide

sentences.text: and by the end of the month, Jack is the one pulling the levers.
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: A train toots its whistle, and Jack grabs the right key and hands it up to the driver.
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: Then one day a lady looks out of her train window and sees a baboon running the railway,
sentences.subject: lady

sentences.text: and she screams so loud that the whole carriage writes to the railway boss.
sentences.subject: lady

sentences.text: So an inspector shows up, looks at the baboon, looks at the signalman, and goes,
sentences.subject: inspector

sentences.text: "You've got a monkey running my trains?"
sentences.subject: inspector

sentences.text: The signalman just smiles and says, "Send one."
sentences.subject: wide

sentences.text: So the inspector sends train after train, and he even mixes up the whistles to trick him.
sentences.subject: inspector

sentences.text: Two toots, Jack throws the lever, four toots, the right key, he doesn't even look up,
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: and by the last train the inspector is the one checking his notes.
sentences.subject: inspector

sentences.text: You see, every driver whistled a different number of times for every track,
sentences.subject: train

sentences.text: kind of like how you know your mom's knock from the mailman's,
sentences.subject: wide

sentences.text: and Jack had learned every single one just by listening.
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: So the inspector goes back to his office and writes the strangest letter the railway ever sent.
sentences.subject: inspector

sentences.text: Jack is hired, twenty cents a day and half a bottle of beer every week,
sentences.subject: jack

sentences.text: and in nine years on the job, he never made a single mistake.
sentences.subject: jack
